quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Protect your account after using a library computer.
quests.explanation: As nouns they become one word: the login page, a logout button. 'Sign in' and 'sign out' mean the same.
quests.textToSpeak: After the security update finishes overnight, you'll need to *log in* again on every device.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: What is the hidden reason behind a fever that keeps coming back?
quests.explanation: Managers borrow it for repeated problems: find the root cause instead of patching the symptom.
quests.textToSpeak: When a patient keeps getting fevers, a good doctor doesn't just treat the *symptom*.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Once every attendee has agreed, the email uses this word.
quests.explanation: 'Provisional' is a formal synonym of tentative.
quests.textToSpeak: Until everyone confirms, please treat the Friday slot as *tentative* for now.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Saving a file from a website onto your laptop.
quests.explanation: Think 'up' for sending and 'down' for receiving: that's an easy way to remember upload and download.
quests.textToSpeak: To be marked on time, please *upload* your assignment before midnight on Friday.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Walk, cycle, and play sport every day and you're this.
quests.explanation: 'Sedentary' comes from the Latin for sitting, so its opposite, 'active', means moving regularly.
quests.textToSpeak: Office workers with a *sedentary* lifestyle should try short walks between meetings.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Could it have been half the length? Then it was this.
quests.explanation: 'Verbose' is the formal word, and 'long-winded' is informal.
quests.textToSpeak: Unlike her manager, her emails are always *concise*, usually just two lines.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Features that keep distracting you get this treatment.
quests.explanation: 'Deactivate' is formal, and 'turn off' is the everyday phrasal version.
quests.textToSpeak: To stop missing messages, go to settings and *enable* notifications for the app.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: A train timetable that never changes.
quests.explanation: 'Set in stone' is the idiom for a plan that can't change.
quests.textToSpeak: Our timetable is *flexible*, so we can meet whenever suits you.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: When a service shows up as a line on your bill, it's this.
quests.explanation: Don't mix it up with 'complementary' (with an e), which means going well together.
quests.textToSpeak: As part of the summer promotion, every guest at the hotel receives *complimentary* breakfast.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Headphones that never tangle in your bag.
quests.explanation: 'Cordless' is used for phones and tools, and Wi-Fi is a wireless network.
quests.textToSpeak: Before the renovation, the old office had *wired* internet in every room.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: For a condition you live with for years, use this word.
quests.explanation: Everyday speech uses 'acute' for severe too: acute pain.
quests.textToSpeak: After collapsing at work, he was taken to hospital with *acute* bronchitis.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Which version goes out to the client?
quests.explanation: 'Finalise' is the verb for making a version complete.
quests.textToSpeak: This is only a *draft*, so please don't share it outside the team.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: With the right key, a coded message gets this.
quests.explanation: 'Unencrypted' means never protected at all, so it isn't quite the same.
quests.textToSpeak: To comply with the privacy law, all patient files must be *encrypted* before they are emailed.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Pension plans are built for this horizon.
quests.explanation: Hyphenate before a noun: a long-term plan.
quests.textToSpeak: Whatever the risks, the board is only interested in *short-term* profits.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: At the bottom of a marketing email, you can stop the messages.
quests.explanation: 'Unsubscribe' is the specific action for mailing lists, and 'opt in' is the opposite of opt out.
quests.textToSpeak: To receive our weekly offers, you can *sign up* for the newsletter on our homepage.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: You want to see the whole country, not just your street.
quests.explanation: Outside screens, 'zoom in on' means focusing on one detail.
quests.textToSpeak: To read the street names properly, use two fingers to *zoom in* on the map.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: A week of night shifts leaves you like this.
quests.explanation: 'Shattered' is British informal, while 'worn out' is common everywhere.
quests.textToSpeak: After a full night's sleep and a slow breakfast, she felt *well-rested*.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: It arrives sooner but costs more.
quests.explanation: 'Priority' and 'next-day' are shop labels for faster options.
quests.textToSpeak: At checkout, the fee for *standard* delivery is three dollars.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: How do you feel on the stairs after a year without exercise?
quests.explanation: 'Fit' also means suitable: fit for purpose.
quests.textToSpeak: She's *fit* enough to climb ten flights of stairs without stopping.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Copying a paragraph and claiming it as your own.
quests.explanation: Americans spell it 'plagiarize'.
quests.textToSpeak: To avoid losing marks, always *cite* your sources at the end of the essay.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Which kind of desk has a person greeting every customer?
quests.explanation: 'Full-service' describes businesses where employees serve you, like some petrol stations.
quests.textToSpeak: To reduce queues at busy hours, the pharmacy has a *self-service* checkout at the front.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Software that keeps its code secret and owned by a company.
quests.explanation: 'Closed-source' is the everyday tech term.
quests.textToSpeak: Because the code is published online, the software is *open source*, so anyone can edit it.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: What good teachers want you to do with an idea, beyond repeating it.
quests.explanation: 'Learn by heart' is the idiom for memorise.
quests.textToSpeak: In the week before the test, it's tempting to *memorise* every formula without knowing what it means.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: What managers report when the deadline is slipping.
quests.explanation: A third option exists: ahead of schedule.
quests.textToSpeak: The project is *on schedule* and should finish next week.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Saving only to your laptop's hard drive.
quests.explanation: 'On-premises' is the business word for local servers.
quests.textToSpeak: Our photos are stored in the *cloud*, so your phone has more free space.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Someone with a diploma from a design school.
quests.explanation: 'Qualified' means holding an official certificate.
quests.textToSpeak: She's *self-taught*, but her design work rivals that of any graduate.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: What the agent hopes to do before the ticket reaches a manager.
quests.explanation: 'De-escalate' is a different word: it means calming a situation.
quests.textToSpeak: The help desk will *escalate* the issue if it can't be solved today.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Numbers on a screen instead of hands make a clock this.
quests.explanation: The British spelling is 'analogue'.
quests.textToSpeak: In the older university laboratory, the lab still uses *analog* instruments for some measurements.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Trucks leaving the depot.
quests.explanation: 'Incoming' and 'outgoing' mean nearly the same.
quests.textToSpeak: Customs officers check *inbound* freight before it reaches the warehouse.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Criticism that only tears people down.
quests.explanation: 'Harsh' focuses on tone, while 'unhelpful' is milder.
quests.textToSpeak: Because it named specific problems and offered solutions, the manager's *constructive* feedback helped everyone improve.
